title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (from pp. 89-91): Grothendieck is working with profinite groups M_{ρ,σ}. These are extensions of an arithmetic group Γ_{ρ,σ} (built from the extended Galois group Γ_Q^~) by a geometric profinite group, written G^+ or 𝔖^+. The next page identifies the universal case M = N_{1,1}^~ as an extension of Γ_Q^~ by SL(2,Z)^. So M_{ρ,σ} is a generalized 'arithmetic modular group': an arithmetic fundamental group of a (twisted) form of the stack M_{1,1}, or of a related orbifold curve with elliptic points of orders ρ and σ.

The subgroups M_{ρ,σ}(0), [0], (1/2), (-j) appear to be decomposition/stabilizer subgroups attached to special points in a λ-type coordinate. λ = 1/2 corresponds to j = 1728 (automorphism group μ_4). λ = -j (a primitive 6th root of unity) corresponds to j = 0 (automorphism group μ_6). These are 'Galois sections with inertia', i.e. stack-inertia decompositions at points with extra automorphisms.

Previous page:
- M_{ρ,σ}(-j) meets μ_ρ trivially.
- Hence one passes to the tilde quotient M~ := M_{ρ,σ}/μ_ρ and Γ~ := Γ/μ_ρ, with M~(-j) the isomorphic image of M_{ρ,σ}(-j).

This page:
- (208) gives an exact sequence 1 → μ_G → M~(-J) → Γ~ → 1. Since μ_G is (presumably) of order 2, M~(-J) is a 'bisection' of M~ → Γ~: a degree-2 multisection rather than a section.
- Define M'~(-J) := M~(-J) ∩ M~^⊊, where M~^⊊ := M^⊊/μ_ρ.
- (209) M'~(-J) maps isomorphically onto Γ'~ := Ker(ε_2 : Γ~ → μ_2). So it is a genuine partial section over an index-2 subgroup. Index check: M'~(-J) has index 4 in M~(-J), namely 2 from the kernel μ_G and 2 from Γ'~ ⊂ Γ~.
- (210) The kernels of the character ε_2 on M~ and on M~^⊊ decompose as products M'~(-J)·G^+ and M'~(-J)·M, i.e. semidirect splittings over the index-2 subgroup.
- Margin NB: Γ~ → N_ρ/μ_ρ is an epimorphism whose kernel is Ker(N_σ → ...) ≅ G_σ. This expresses Γ~ as a kind of diagonal/fibre product of the N_ρ and N_σ data.

Remark: one should develop interesting subgroups of M~(-J), to be revisited for general M_{ρ,σ}. The next page then turns to notation: the quotient groups M/μ_ρ are 'the most interesting' and deserve the plain symbol.

Purpose: to understand how the special points (elliptic points with automorphisms μ_4, μ_6) give sections or multisections of the arithmetic modular group over Galois. These are the 'stack inertia' versions of Galois sections at tangential/rational base points, which feed the Teichmüller-tower/Grothendieck–Teichmüller programme of La Longue Marche.
errors: No mathematical error is visible. The index bookkeeping is consistent: 2 × 2 = 4.

There is a minor inconsistency in the text: 'd'image Γ'~ d'indice 2 dans Γ'_{ρ,σ}' should presumably read 'd'indice 2 dans Γ~_{ρ,σ}', since by (209) Γ'~ is the kernel of ε_2 on Γ~. It may be a notational slip; the transcription is uncertain.

ideas.what: Decomposition subgroups at elliptic points (j=0, j=1728) of the arithmetic fundamental group of M_{1,1}-type orbifolds, viewed as (multi)sections over the Galois group, with the automorphism group (stack inertia) as kernel
ideas.modern_name: Galois sections / decomposition groups at points with nontrivial stack inertia; Galois action on stack inertia
ideas.usually_credited_to: Nakamura and Ihara–Nakamura (Galois action on π1 of M_{1,1}); Collas–Maugeais (Galois action on stack inertia, 2010s)
ideas.where_published: Only hinted at in Esquisse d'un programme (role of points with extra automorphisms in the Teichmüller tower); the detailed computation is unpublished (Longue Marche sequel)

ideas.what: Quotienting by μ_ρ so that the stabilizer of the j=0 point becomes a bisection, then a true section over the index-2 kernel of a character ε_2; semidirect decompositions (210)
ideas.modern_name: Splitting of the arithmetic modular group over an index-2 subgroup of Galois via an elliptic-point section

ideas.what: Description of Γ~ as mapping onto N_ρ/μ_ρ with kernel ≅ G_σ (fibre-product structure)

missed.claim: Grothendieck flags a systematic study of 'interesting subgroups' of the elliptic-point decomposition groups M~(-J) for general M_{ρ,σ}, and plans to return to it. This is an early, explicit programme on the Galois action at points with stack inertia in genus-1 moduli. It anticipates later work (Collas–Maugeais on Galois action on stack inertia) but is not developed here.
missed.quote: Il conviendrait de [?] dans le développement de sous-groupes intéressants de M~_{ρ,σ}(-J) — j'y reviendrai encore une fois, sans doute, dans le contexte des relations en groupes M_{ρ,σ} généraux.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Elliptic-point stabilizers and their Galois sections enter the study of torsion in GT^ and of 'special loci' in the Teichmüller tower. Grothendieck's treatment of general (ρ,σ) and of quotients by μ_ρ could suggest further structure, but the page itself gives no new theorem.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a technically detailed, unpublished treatment of the sections and bisections defined by the j=0 elliptic point in arithmetic modular groups. It is conceptually prefigured by Esquisse and later developed independently (Nakamura, Collas–Maugeais). The computations themselves are routine group-theoretic bookkeeping.
transcription_corrections: Line 2 of the page reads 'M~_{ρ,σ}(-½) [or (-J)] est une bisection de' — the symbol after M~ is an abbreviated 'est', not '[?]'.
In (209), the target of ε_2 appears to be 'μ_2' (subscript partly scratched).

The margin NB reads roughly: 'NB On a Γ~_{ρ,σ} → N_ρ/μ_ρ épi de noyau Ker(N_σ → Θ_{12}) ≃ G_σ et donc ... diagonale, i.e. ... Γ~_{ρ,σ} → N_ρ/μ_ρ ... le diagramme ... de sous-groupes ... dans M~_{ρ,σ}(-J) on trouve ...'
